cmad.notes: SOHO is an operational, NASA-co-funded mission (NASA is responsible for mission operations at GSFC and the mission is still returning data as of 2026-08-16), so a CMAD is expected. None located. Searched: (a) the SPASE NASA/Document registry (only ICON and MMS have CMAD document records; https://spase-metadata.org/NASA/Document/ returns 404 for a SOHO subdirectory); (b) the SOHO project site data/archive and publications pages (https://soho.nascom.nasa.gov/data/archive/ and https://soho.nascom.nasa.gov/publications/ - the latter posts 2001/2003/2005 Senior Review proposals but no CMAD); (c) general web search and a Zenodo API search for 'CMAD SOHO' (only unrelated SOHO/EPHIN and ERNE calibration datasets). Absence is a notable gap: current-team evidence for this run therefore came from the SOHO mission People page's 'SOHO PIs' table instead of a CMAD front page.

instrument_coverage.notes: Reverse lookup of https://spase-metadata.org/SMWG/Instrument/SOHO/ returned 13 records; every one was verified to carry ObservatoryID = spase://SMWG/Observatory/SOHO. Twelve are payload instruments and match the external roster exactly; the thirteenth (SOHO/Ephemeris, 'SOHO Positions', InstrumentType=Platform) is a spacecraft-ephemeris pseudo-instrument with no PI and no description paper, so it contributes no instrument leads. The external roster was taken from the SOHO mission Instruments page and cross-checked against the About page ('The twelve instruments on board SOHO...'), the Observatory record's own Description ('Twelve instruments comprised the payload'), and the mission overview paper. All three agree: no instrument is missing from SPASE. Each of the 12 instruments has a dedicated description paper in the Solar Physics 162 (1995) SOHO special issue, all of which were retrieved from Crossref and processed.

Mission-overview paper selection CONFIDENT: Domingo, Fleck & Poland 1995, 'The SOHO mission: An overview', Solar Phys. 162, 1-37 (10.1007/BF00733425). Passes every heuristic - title keyword 'overview', names the observatory, published the same month as launch, and 1506 citations per OpenAlex. Crossref and OpenAlex agree on the author list, and the two variant SOHO overview papers OpenAlex returns for 1995 (Space Sci. Rev. and the Solar Phys. reprint) have the identical three authors, so the selection cannot change who is taken. Semantic Scholar was rate-limited (HTTP 429) on every attempt; OpenAlex was used as the second literature index in its place.
Author-order detection, mission overview: n=3, longest sorted suffix = 3, which is below the 5-name threshold, so the list is treated as NOT alphabetized and positions 1-3 are Strong.

Author-order detection, instrument papers (backward scan on normalized family names): CDS n=39 suffix 1; CELIAS n=33 suffix 1; COSTEP n=19 suffix 1; EIT n=28 suffix 3; ERNE n=15 suffix 6 from position 10 (partially alphabetized, prefix = positions 1-9); GOLF n=31 suffix 1; LASCO n=15 suffix 2; MDI n=12 suffix 6 from position 7 (partially alphabetized, prefix = positions 1-6); SUMER n=16 suffix 2; SWAN n=25 suffix 1; UVCS n=40 suffix 2; VIRGO n=25 suffix 4. Only ERNE and MDI are partially alphabetized, and in both the prefix is longer than three, so positions 1-3 were taken from the prefix in every case. No paper was fully alphabetized.

Instrument-paper selection CONFIDENT for all twelve: each is the dedicated description paper in the Solar Physics 162 (1995) SOHO special issue, published the month of launch, with a large team author list, the instrument named in the title, and high citation counts (LASCO 2824, MDI 2413, EIT 1787, SUMER 797, CDS 573, UVCS 437, VIRGO 309, CELIAS 295, GOLF 237, ERNE 225, COSTEP 222 per OpenAlex). Three of the DOIs (CELIAS, COSTEP, ERNE) are cited by the SPASE Instrument records themselves, which anchors the whole contiguous DOI series.

Observatory scoping rule applied strictly and symmetrically: from each instrument paper only positions 1-3 (or prefix positions 1-3) were taken, at Strong. Every author at position 4 or beyond on all twelve instrument papers was excluded as instrument-team depth belonging to that Instrument record's own finder run - 262 people in total (298 authors across the twelve papers, minus the 36 taken), not enumerated individually. Three of them (Berndt Klecker, CELIAS 4; J. Todd Hoeksema, MDI 4; Philippe Lemaire, SUMER 5) are nevertheless included here, but only because an INDEPENDENT source earns it for them - a retired provider PI listing for Klecker, and lead authorship of the 1992 ESA SP-348 description paper the Instrument record itself cites for Hoeksema and Lemaire. Their instrument-paper position was not used.

Second description-paper generation: eight Instrument record Descriptions cite an earlier design-phase paper from the First SOHO Workshop (ESA SP-348, November 1992). Where such a citation names an individual not already captured, that individual was included at Medium as a named lead of a record-cited description paper: Hoeksema (MDI), Lemaire (SUMER), Noci (UVCS). The full author lists of those proceedings papers could not be retrieved (they are cited as 'et al.'), so only the explicitly named individuals were taken, and at Medium rather than Strong.

SPASE Instrument Contacts are systematically out of date relative to the provider's current PI table. Of the twelve payload records, only four name the current PI (CELIAS/Wimmer-Schweingruber, COSTEP/Heber, ERNE/Vainio, MDI/Scherrer). The other eight name the founding-generation PI: CDS/Harrison (now Fludra), EIT/Delaboudiniere (now Auchere), GOLF/Gabriel (now Boumier), LASCO/Howard (now Battams), SUMER/Wilhelm (now Curdt), SWAN/Bertaux (now Quemerais), UVCS/Kohl (now Strachan), VIRGO/Froehlich (now Finsterle). Those eight are recorded with role FormerPI, sourced to the Instrument record Contacts plus the superseding provider listing, rather than PrincipalInvestigator - emitting PrincipalInvestigator for them would assert a role the live provider page contradicts. This is a curation finding worth passing back to SMWG.

The SOHO People page's 'SOHO PIs' table also preserves four retired PI entries as HTML comments (Klecker/CELIAS, Bertaux/SWAN, Torsti/ERNE, Valtonen/ERNE). These were read as Medium FormerPI evidence: the entry is on the provider's official page but explicitly retired.

FLAG for the reviewer: the UVCS Instrument record lists TWO PrincipalInvestigators, John L. Kohl and J. Leonard Culhane. Culhane's documented SOHO involvement is with CDS/MSSL - he appears at position 15 of the CDS instrument paper (misspelled 'J. L. Gulhane' in the Crossref record) and nowhere in the UVCS author list. The UVCS PI entry for him is very probably a SPASE metadata error. He is included at Medium because a qualifying contact role is Medium evidence by rule, but this entry should be verified (and the UVCS record corrected) before he is written into any DOI.

A companion paper to the mission overview exists - 'SOHO ground segment, science operations, and data products', Solar Phys. 162, 39 (10.1007/BF00733426), 5 authors. It is a ground-segment/operations paper, not the observatory description paper, so no position-based evidence was drawn from it. Joseph Gurman appears on it, but his inclusion here rests on the independent NASA/SDAC provider pages naming him US SOHO Project Scientist.

Vicente Domingo and Arthur Poland are widely described as the founding ESA and NASA SOHO project scientists respectively, but no source fetched during this run states that role for either of them explicitly, so neither carries a ProjectScientist role here - only Author. Bernhard Fleck and Jack Ireland carry ProjectScientist because the Observatory record's own Contacts names it.

Charra, R. I. Bush, E. Marsch, E. Kyroelae, R. Esser, L. D. Gardner, G. Noci) no expansion was invented; downstream name resolution will be needed before Person records can be matched or created.
